title: Esquiva 3D — swap procedural cubes for Kenney CC0 models (hero, enemies, dungeon floor)
description: Integrate the reference-assets Kenney packs (CC0) into the Esquiva 3D demo, replacing the procedurally-generated primitive cubes with real low-poly models: an animal-cube hero for the player, character-cube models for the chaser obstacles, and Mini Dungeon floor tiles for the collapsing arena. Visual-only change — the Core dodge rules (GridArena/DodgeSim) are untouched; the swap happens in the View/Bootstrap layer. Integration MUST be GUID-free and headless-safe: load models via Resources.Load by path with a primitive-cube fallback when a model is missing, so the fast suite and any headless build keep working. Packs: reference-assets-chars (Cube Pets, players), reference-assets-enemy (character-a..r, enemies), reference-assets-stage (Mini Dungeon, level). All CC0 (commercial OK, credit Kenney optional).
acceptance_criteria: Selected FBX models + shared colormap.png are copied under a Resources/ folder in the Unity project (e.g. Assets/Barcade/Art/DodgeModels/Resources/...) so they load by path at runtime with no scene/GUID wiring
DodgeGameBootstrap instantiates a hero model for the player, distinct character models for the obstacle/chaser cubes, and a Mini Dungeon floor model for arena tiles — each loaded via Resources.Load
If a model fails to load (null), the original GameObject.CreatePrimitive(Cube) path is used as fallback so headless/test runs never break
Model instances are scaled/rotated to fit one grid tile and centered correctly; the existing collapse/fall/sync animations still drive the root transform unchanged
Player, enemies, and floor are visually distinguishable from each other
Fast dotnet suite stays green (Core rules unchanged)
reference-assets-chars/ reference-assets-enemy/ reference-assets-stage/ are committed to the repo as the asset source of truth
